checked_classes: False core-completion claims — Core closure is explicitly based on the operator’s scope revision and exact-installer acceptance, not independent certification of every runtime predicate or whole-portfolio completion.

Representation qualification miscredited — The plan revision, reflection, final candidate record and follow-up explicitly exclude representation from core closure and retain C17 as unqualified; neither approval nor native challenge resolution is treated as successful read/disclosure.

Missing preserved evidence — The packet records a passing check that 19 preserved copies match original hashes, identifies their repository manifest, retains both attempt identities and approval references, and records a passing acceptance-unchanged check.

Counter or denominator changes — Closeout retains historical code completion at 61/61 tasks and 20/20 changes, portfolio accounting at 43/61 terminal with 42 qualified and one skipped duplicate, and Cadence at 17 successful deliveries with zero closeout delivery credit.

Source and payload identity conflation — Exact public installer identities are recorded separately for each platform; earlier local and historical operations retain their original payload identities and are described as source-contract applicability rather than operations on public bytes.

Acceptance and publication conflation — The acceptance receipt labels installed operation as operator-reported, explicitly disclaims independently observed native Windows execution, and separates publication evidence from installed acceptance.

Historical pending records presented as current blockers — Earlier pending coverage and acceptance receipts remain unchanged historical snapshots; the later closeout revision explicitly supersedes pending-core wording and separately dispositions unresolved representation.

Unintended authority or new operation requirements — Closeout authorizes administrative completion and commit/push, prohibits further approval/read cycles, and preserves the rule that expired challenges and synthetic grants confer no replay or real organizational authority.

Premature lifecycle success claims — The final candidate record distinguishes approved scope closure from lead-owned canonical transitions, and the reflection states that verification, archive and restoration are recorded only after commands succeed.
